original_question: For generalized exponential families such as q-exponential or lambda-exponential families, is there a systematic way to treat the deformation parameter itself as an additional parameter rather than fixing it in advance?
target_in_paper: Section 8, item 1 (Ting-Kam Leonard Wong): the open problem asking whether the deformation parameter in a generalized exponential family should itself be studied as an additional parameter, in the specific setting where varying that parameter produces a foliated statistical manifold whose leaves are the fixed-parameter families. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core target very well: it identifies the right topic (generalized exponential families), the paper’s motivating examples (the q-exponential / λ-exponential setting), and the main issue that the literature usually fixes the deformation parameter in advance while the paper asks what happens if one varies it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The paper does not ask this for generalized exponential families in full undifferentiated generality; it singles out as the key example the q-exponential family reparameterized as a λ-exponential family in equation (3). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The nearby context says that, for each fixed deformation parameter, the corresponding λ-exponential family M_λ is already well behaved; under suitable regularity conditions it carries a natural dualistic geometry with constant sectional curvature. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The official formulation is geometric, not merely parametric: varying the deformation parameter leads to a foliated statistical manifold M whose leaves are the fixed-parameter families. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper’s sharpened question is whether the total space M can be given a natural geometric structure that is useful for statistical inference; that inferential-geometric aim is missing from the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper explicitly points to nearby prior work constructing a divergence on a foliation by deformed probability simplexes, which helps pin down the intended direction without broadening the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

A paper-faithful rewrite should avoid inventing extra assumptions on the parameter range or regularity hypotheses beyond the paper’s own wording ('under suitable regularity conditions'). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: In the specific setting where the q-exponential family is reparameterized as a λ-exponential family and each fixed deformation parameter yields a well-behaved leaf M_λ that, under suitable regularity conditions, carries a natural dualistic geometry of constant sectional curvature, can one systematically treat the deformation parameter itself as an additional parameter by viewing the resulting collection of models as a foliated statistical manifold M and endowing the total space M with a natural geometric structure useful for statistical inference? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because your draft matches the first sentence of Section 8, item 1 almost verbatim, and the immediately adjacent context supplies exactly the extra scope that makes the question paper-faithful: the q-exponential-to-λ-exponential example, the fixed-parameter constant-curvature geometry under suitable regularity conditions, the foliated-manifold viewpoint, and the final aim of obtaining a natural geometry useful for inference. The paper is a collection of open problems, so Section 8, item 1 is the correct target rather than any theorem-style statement elsewhere. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
